collections/ordering#

Stable ordered sequences and binary-search projections.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let empty is List<int> = EmptyList();
let numbers = Sorted(origin: empty.prefix(2).prefix(1).prefix(3));
numbers.first();               // 1
numbers.last();                // 3
numbers.item(1);               // 2

Description#

Stable ordered sequences and binary-search projections.

Sorted orders an Iterating source by the value's own Comparing<T> implementation. It sorts on the first question and keeps the order:

SortedBy applies a key once per input value, decorates the value with Ranked, and routes the complete decorated array through the same host bulk sort. Equal keys retain their input order:

let by_priority = SortedBy(
    origin: jobs,
    key: (job is Job) is int { job.priority(); },
);

The anonymous action's declared result (is int) supplies K (#214); a named bound action with an exact (T) is K type does the same.

Ranked is also useful directly when a domain ordering must differ from a value's intrinsic ordering. Its order() delegates only to key.order().

LowerBound and UpperBound return insertion positions in O(log n). PositionOf returns the first matching position and throws MissingItem when the value is absent:

let first_two = LowerBound(origin: numbers, item: 2).index();
let after_twos = UpperBound(origin: numbers, item: 2).index();
let exact = PositionOf(origin: numbers, item: 2).index();

Binary-search objects require an ascending Sequencing value produced under the same Comparing policy. They deliberately do not spend O(n) validating that precondition on every O(log n) query.
